To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the difficulties of object- oriented development techniques are primarily due to the need for developers to change how they think about the software development process and how they work together as a team to develop software.
the difficulties of using object-oriented techniques are primarily related to the lack of appropriate training and experience.

(1) the difficulties of using object-oriented (OO ) techniques can be identified using a group cognitive mapping process, and (2) the issues that cause difficulties are perceived by novices, experts, and intermediates to be the same but their causal relationships are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the difficulties associated with using OO system development techniques and with the perceptions of developers who use OO system development techniques.
identifying and understanding the difficulties of using object-oriented (OO), system development techniques and the causal relationships between these difficulties.
the identification of the difficult issues of OO system development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the difficulties of using object-oriented development techniques are not limited to the novice, but that there is a common set of issues that all levels of developers face.
the issues perceived as difficult by developers are similar, regardless of experience, but that experts and novices differ in the causal relationships they perceive between issues.
there were no significant differences in the difficulties experienced by novices, experts, or intermediates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the difficulties of using object-oriented techniques are not limited to the learning curve of the novice.
there is a core of difficult issues associated to the use of OO techniques.
there are a core of common issues that are perceived by all developers as difficult, and that there is a difference between the perceptions of experts and novices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the difficulties of using object-oriented development techniques are shared across levels of experience and that the difficulties are not just a novice phenomenon.

there is a "core" set of difficult issues that all developers face, and that there are differences in the causal relations between the difficult issues perceived by novices, experts, and intermediates.

the difficulties of using object-oriented techniques are not just a matter of learning new concepts, but are a result of the complexity of the concepts, their interrelationships, and the difficulty of applying them in practice.
